The doc comment on detail_from_job_logs in client.rs says the same, and so do the comments on without_post_job_cleanup and failure_tail in checks.rs.

FAILED` and `test result: FAILED`, and assert_no_cleanup checks that no cleanup text is present. The test uses only `stamped` (gh/tests.rs line 376, an unchanged line, so it exists on base) and the public detail_from_job_logs and FailureDetail fields, so it should compile on base. criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core detail_from_job_logs`: a test with a multi-line panic message longer than 4 lines asserts the whole message survives in output_tail.

The longest is the 4-line assert_eq message in failing_unit_lines, and it sits near the end of a short log, so the plain tail keeps it anyway. The code also still caps each block: checks.rs line 274 has `end <= m + FAILURE_BLOCK_AFTER` with FAILURE_BLOCK_AFTER = 4. So the fix the reading promised for Finding 2 (extend a block until a blank line or the next `----` header, within the n/2 cap) was not made. Lines after the fourth are lost whenever the failure lies outside the end window.

findings.summary: Finding 2 from the earlier job is not fixed: a failure block is still the marker plus at most 4 lines, and there is no test for a panic message longer than 4 lines (criterion 4).
findings.evidence: `const FAILURE_BLOCK_AFTER: usize = 4;` and `while end < lines.len() && end <= m + FAILURE_BLOCK_AFTER && !lines[end].trim().is_empty()`. The reading promised to extend a block until a blank line or the next `----` header, within the n/2 cap. None of the 3 tests in gh/tests.rs has a panic message longer than 4 lines. The simpler, correct rule: drop the fixed count and end a block at the first blank line or the next `---- ... ----` header, keeping the n/2 cap that already exists.

findings.summary: I could only confirm by reading the code that the new tests fail on base, not by running them.
findings.evidence: The tests use only `stamped` (existing, line 376) and the public detail_from_job_logs, so they should compile on base, and on base the cleanup lines would make assert_no_cleanup fail. This role may not check out base, so the tests were not run there.

findings.summary: The 480-byte end window is a guess at what readers see, not a value taken from those readers.
findings.evidence: `const FAILURE_END_WINDOW_BYTES: usize = 480;` and its doc says "end-keeping readers are sure to see". Nothing ties it to the actual cut sizes in introspection or the verifier brief. Deriving it from those cuts, or always moving failure blocks to the end, would remove the guess.

summary: The verdict is fail. The retry still keeps only 4 lines after each failure line, which was the main finding (Finding 2) of the earlier job, and the test that should catch this is missing. For a failure early in the log, any panic message longer than 4 lines is still cut. I ran the three new detail_from_job_logs tests and the 18 tail-related tests, and all pass. Athena's fmt, clippy and test checks also passed on this tree. The rest of the change works: each CI log is now cut before its post-job cleanup, failure lines from earlier in the log are moved to the end of the stored tail, and both CHANGELOG.md and the code comments name the root cause. The four changed files are exactly the expected ones. By reading the code I believe the new tests compile on base and fail there on the cleanup assertions, but I could not run them on base because this role may not check out other commits. The fix is to end a block at the first blank line or the next `---- ... ----` header, within the existing half-of-the-lines cap, and to add a gh test whose early panic message runs longer than 4 lines.
